title: THC Academy
subtitle: Practice the system, not just the vocabulary.
learningOutcome: Move from observation to measurement, interpretation, action, and verification across the major cannabis plant-science and cultivation systems without relying on universal recipes or single-symptom guesses.
studyRules: Record what you observed before writing what you think caused it.
Preserve units, sampling method, location, time, plant stage, and recent changes with every measurement.
Change one controllable variable at a time when practical, then verify the response before stacking another change.
Treat cultivar, environment, media, water, equipment, and measurement method as context rather than assuming one universal target.
Use the linked V6 subject page as the reference layer when an exercise exposes a knowledge gap.

courses.title: Evidence, Observation & Records
courses.purpose: Build the measurement habits that make every later Academy course more reliable.
courses.evidenceBoundary: A measurement is only comparable when method and context are comparable. Precision does not prove accuracy, and correlation does not by itself prove cause.

units.title: Observation versus interpretation
units.task: Write a plant observation using only visible or measured facts, then write three possible interpretations separately.
units.verify: A second reader can distinguish facts from hypotheses without guessing.

units.title: Accuracy, precision and calibration
units.task: Create a calibration log for one meter or sensor and record standard, date, result, adjustment and acceptance decision.
units.verify: The record shows what standard was used and whether the instrument was accepted or held.

units.title: Sampling and sensor placement
units.task: Map at least four measurement locations and state why each location represents a different question or risk.
units.verify: The map can be repeated by another person using the written positions.

units.title: Baselines and change control
units.task: Choose one variable and define the baseline period, planned change, hold conditions and follow-up window before making the change.
units.verify: The record makes it possible to compare before and after without relying on memory.

units.title: Standardized photos and timelines
units.task: Create a repeatable photo protocol with plant ID, angle, distance, lighting condition and date/time fields.
units.verify: Two photo sessions can be compared without major framing or identity ambiguity.

exercises.title: Build a one-page observation form
exercises.deliverable: A reusable form containing plant ID, stage, location, measurements, symptoms, recent changes, photos, hypotheses, action and verification date.

exercises.title: Audit a strong-sounding claim
exercises.deliverable: A short claim audit separating the claim, evidence actually shown, missing controls, uncertainty and what additional observation would strengthen it.

courses.capstone: Document one small cultivation change from baseline through follow-up using measurements, photos, a stated hypothesis and an explicit conclusion that preserves uncertainty.
completion: I can separate observation from diagnosis.
I record method and units with measurements.
I can describe a baseline and comparison window.
I preserve uncertainty when evidence is incomplete.

courses.title: Plant Biology & Anatomy
courses.purpose: Use anatomy and physiology to explain what a plant can sense, move, build and repair.
courses.evidenceBoundary: Visible structure supports biological interpretation, but one visual feature rarely proves a physiological mechanism without additional measurements.

units.title: Organs and functional roles
units.task: Label roots, stems, nodes, leaves, shoot tips and reproductive structures on a real plant or reference image and write one primary function for each.
units.verify: Labels and functions match the actual structure rather than grower slang.

units.title: Transport pathways
units.task: Trace a conceptual path for water/minerals from root to leaf and for assimilated carbon from source leaves to sinks.
units.verify: The diagram distinguishes xylem transport from phloem allocation.

units.title: Meristems and architecture
units.task: Map the active shoot and axillary growth points on one plant before any training action.
units.verify: The map predicts which sites could continue growth if the main apex changes.

units.title: Stomata, leaves and gas exchange
units.task: List the environmental variables that change leaf gas exchange and identify which can be measured in your setup.
units.verify: The list includes light, leaf/air conditions and water status rather than only room RH.

units.title: Trichomes and reproductive tissues
units.task: Compare glandular trichomes, stigmas, bracts and leaf tissue using magnification and record what each observation can and cannot establish.
units.verify: The notes do not treat one visual cue as a complete maturity or chemistry test.

exercises.title: Build a plant anatomy field sheet
exercises.deliverable: A labeled specimen or photo sheet with organ, function, observation and uncertainty columns.

exercises.title: Explain one symptom through anatomy
exercises.deliverable: A short mechanism map connecting the symptom location to the tissues and transport processes that could plausibly be involved.

courses.capstone: Create a one-page whole-plant systems diagram connecting roots, transport, leaves, meristems, reproductive structures and environmental inputs.
completion: I can identify major organs and growth points.
I can distinguish xylem and phloem roles.
I can connect anatomy to cultivation observations.
I avoid using visual anatomy as proof of unmeasured chemistry.

courses.title: Lifecycle & Propagation
courses.purpose: Match decisions to developmental stage and release propagated plants by observed readiness rather than elapsed days alone.
courses.evidenceBoundary: Development rate varies with genotype, environment, root condition and propagation method; calendar age alone is not a universal release criterion.

units.title: Stage identification
units.task: Define observable criteria for germination, seedling establishment, vegetative growth, reproductive transition and maturation.
units.verify: Each stage has observable criteria rather than only an age range.

units.title: Seed and seedling establishment
units.task: Track one establishment batch using identity, start date, emergence, early growth and failure notes.
units.verify: Losses can be traced to individual IDs or batch records.

units.title: Cuttings and donor health
units.task: Create a donor/cutting record that includes source identity, donor condition, sanitation, cutting position and rooting observations.
units.verify: Every cutting can be traced back to a donor and handling event.

units.title: Rooting and acclimation
units.task: Define release criteria for rooted propagules using roots, posture, new growth and water response.
units.verify: Release does not depend on a fixed number of days alone.

units.title: Transition management
units.task: List the measurements that should be rechecked when a plant moves to a new container, light level or environmental zone.
units.verify: The checklist includes both root-zone and canopy/environment measurements.

exercises.title: Propagation batch card
exercises.deliverable: A batch record with source, IDs, dates, method, environment, rooting evidence, losses and release decision.

exercises.title: Stage-change checklist
exercises.deliverable: A transition checklist for one lifecycle move with acceptance criteria and follow-up measurements.

courses.capstone: Follow one plant or propagation batch through two developmental transitions and document what changed in management, measurements and acceptance criteria.
completion: I identify stage from observable development.
I preserve source identity through propagation.
I use readiness criteria for release.
I remeasure after meaningful transitions.

courses.title: Environment & VPD
courses.purpose: Understand the environment as spatial and time-varying rather than one room-average number.
courses.evidenceBoundary: VPD is a useful descriptor of atmospheric demand, not a stand-alone diagnosis. Leaf temperature, air movement, plant water status and sensor location affect interpretation.

units.title: Temperature and RH mapping
units.task: Measure at multiple canopy positions and compare room-average values with interior or edge values.
units.verify: The map preserves location, time and sensor identity.

units.title: Leaf temperature context
units.task: Measure or estimate leaf-temperature differences at representative canopy positions and note what changed the reading.
units.verify: Leaf and air temperature are not treated as interchangeable.

units.title: VPD interpretation
units.task: Calculate or record VPD for two conditions and explain what additional plant information is needed before acting.
units.verify: The conclusion does not treat VPD alone as proof of stress.

units.title: Air movement versus moisture removal
units.task: Identify which equipment circulates air and which equipment actually removes or exchanges moisture.
units.verify: The equipment map separates circulation from dehumidification/ventilation.

units.title: Transitions and risk windows
units.task: Graph or log conditions around lights-on, lights-off or irrigation to find rapid environmental transitions.
units.verify: The record captures a time series rather than one spot reading.

exercises.title: Nine-point climate map
exercises.deliverable: A canopy map showing temperature/RH measurements, sensor positions and the most important spatial differences.

exercises.title: Transition investigation
exercises.deliverable: A short timeline around one environmental transition with suspected cause, observed plant response and follow-up.

courses.capstone: Build an environment characterization for one grow zone using spatial measurements, transition data, equipment states and explicit uncertainty.
completion: I map more than one location.
I distinguish leaf and air temperature.
I use VPD as context, not diagnosis.
I distinguish air movement from moisture removal.

courses.title: Lighting
courses.purpose: Measure the photons reaching the crop and connect intensity, duration, geometry and plant response.
courses.evidenceBoundary: Fixture wattage, hanging height and marketing output do not substitute for crop-plane measurement; usable settings depend on geometry, canopy, environment and cultivar response.

units.title: PPF, PPFD and DLI
units.task: Explain the difference between fixture output, photon density at the crop plane and daily photon exposure.
units.verify: The explanation keeps units and time components distinct.

units.title: Crop-plane mapping
units.task: Measure or plan a repeatable grid across the canopy plane and record fixture state and measurement height.
units.verify: The grid can be repeated after a change.

units.title: Uniformity and edge falloff
units.task: Compare minimum, maximum and average measurements and identify zones that are consistently different.
units.verify: The conclusion does not rely on average PPFD alone.

units.title: Photoperiod and dark integrity
units.task: Document timer/controller schedule and identify possible interruptions or timing drift.
units.verify: The actual schedule is checked rather than assumed from controller settings.

units.title: Light response and heat interaction
units.task: Compare light position with leaf temperature, posture and environmental measurements.
units.verify: A light-related interpretation includes heat/environment context.

exercises.title: Create a PPFD map template
exercises.deliverable: A reusable grid with coordinates, sensor height, fixture settings, raw readings and summary statistics.

exercises.title: Calculate a DLI comparison
exercises.deliverable: Two DLI calculations using measured or hypothetical PPFD and photoperiod, with assumptions shown.

courses.capstone: Characterize one lighting zone with a repeatable PPFD grid, DLI calculation, uniformity summary and plant-response notes.
completion: I distinguish PPF, PPFD and DLI.
I map the crop plane.
I preserve raw readings and geometry.
I connect light changes to environmental and plant response.

courses.title: Water, pH & EC
courses.purpose: Use water chemistry and root-zone measurements as a system instead of treating one pH or EC number as the diagnosis.
courses.evidenceBoundary: pH, EC, alkalinity and hardness describe different properties. Runoff or extract values depend on sampling method and cannot be compared blindly across systems.

units.title: Source-water characterization
units.task: Record source-water pH, EC and available alkalinity/hardness information separately.
units.verify: The record does not treat pH as a measure of alkalinity or mineral concentration.

units.title: Meter control
units.task: Create calibration and storage steps for pH and EC instruments used in the grow.
units.verify: The procedure includes standards, rinsing/storage and acceptance decisions.

units.title: Sampling method
units.task: Define exactly how one feed, root-zone, runoff or extract sample is collected.
units.verify: Another person could repeat the sample method.

units.title: Irrigation and dryback
units.task: Choose a repeatable method for tracking water input and media drying between events.
units.verify: Dryback is defined by a measurement or explicit observation method.

units.title: Trend interpretation
units.task: Plot several sequential readings before deciding whether a value is stable, drifting or an outlier.
units.verify: The interpretation uses a trend rather than one isolated number.

exercises.title: Water profile worksheet
exercises.deliverable: A source-water and irrigation record separating pH, EC, alkalinity/hardness context, treatment and final solution measurements.

exercises.title: Sampling-method comparison
exercises.deliverable: A side-by-side description of two sample methods and why their results should or should not be compared directly.

courses.capstone: Build a seven-day water/root-zone log and explain the observed trends without using a universal target as the only evidence.
completion: I distinguish pH, EC, alkalinity and hardness.
I document calibration.
I state sample method with results.
I interpret trends before isolated readings.

courses.title: Nutrition & Media
courses.purpose: Connect essential elements, media physics, nutrient delivery and plant response without reducing nutrition to a bottle recipe.
courses.evidenceBoundary: Element demand and root-zone behavior depend on cultivar, stage, media, water chemistry, environment and total delivery. Visual symptoms alone rarely identify one nutrient cause with certainty.

units.title: Essential elements and roles
units.task: Group macro- and micronutrients by broad plant roles and note where visual overlap makes diagnosis uncertain.
units.verify: The worksheet separates biological role from symptom folklore.

units.title: Media physical properties
units.task: Describe the media in terms of water retention, aeration, drainage, particle structure and container geometry.
units.verify: The description goes beyond simply naming the media brand/type.

units.title: CEC and buffering context
units.task: Explain how exchange capacity or buffering can affect root-zone chemistry in the chosen media.
units.verify: The explanation avoids assuming all media behave the same way.

units.title: Mixing records and compatibility
units.task: Create a repeatable input log with product, batch, sequence, measured final EC/pH and observations.
units.verify: The log can recreate what was actually mixed without relying on memory.

units.title: Differential nutrition diagnosis
units.task: For one visual symptom, list nutrient and non-nutrient alternatives and what evidence would separate them.
units.verify: At least one environmental/root-zone alternative remains until evidence excludes it.

exercises.title: Media system profile
exercises.deliverable: A profile covering container, media components, drainage/aeration assumptions, irrigation behavior and sampling method.

exercises.title: Nutrient differential table
exercises.deliverable: A symptom comparison table with candidate causes, supporting evidence, conflicting evidence and next measurement.

courses.capstone: Explain one nutrition-related case using media, water, environment, feed records, symptoms and competing hypotheses rather than a single deficiency chart.
completion: I connect nutrients to root-zone context.
I describe media physical behavior.
I keep complete mixing records.
I use differential diagnosis for visual symptoms.

courses.title: Plant Health & IPM
courses.purpose: Turn scouting into mapped evidence and choose controls only after the problem is characterized well enough to act responsibly.
courses.evidenceBoundary: A symptom or trap catch is evidence, not a complete diagnosis. Pest/pathogen identification, environment, distribution and progression should be considered before treatment.

units.title: Mapped scouting
units.task: Create a repeatable scouting route and assign plant/zone/trap identifiers.
units.verify: Findings can be located on a map after the scouting session.

units.title: Abiotic versus biotic patterns
units.task: Compare distribution, progression, tissue age, roots, environment and recent changes for one case.
units.verify: The notes preserve both abiotic and biotic possibilities until evidence separates them.

units.title: Arthropod identification
units.task: Document one arthropod observation with location, life stage if known, magnification/photo and confidence level.
units.verify: The record distinguishes confirmed identification from suspected identification.

units.title: Disease and sanitation boundaries
units.task: Map clean, suspect and affected zones plus tool/person movement controls.
units.verify: The workflow reduces cross-contamination and preserves evidence.

units.title: Control and follow-up
units.task: For any intervention, define label/legal check, target problem, application record and verification date.
units.verify: Success is evaluated with follow-up evidence rather than assuming treatment worked.

exercises.title: Scout a 10-location route
exercises.deliverable: A completed scouting sheet with locations, observations, counts/severity, photos and next actions.

exercises.title: Build a differential diagnosis tree
exercises.deliverable: A decision tree beginning with symptom pattern and separating root, environment, nutrition, arthropod and disease possibilities.

courses.capstone: Investigate a real or simulated plant-health case from intake through differential diagnosis, action criteria and follow-up verification.
completion: I scout on a repeatable map.
I separate evidence from diagnosis.
I preserve quarantine/sanitation boundaries.
I verify outcomes after intervention.

courses.title: Training & Canopy Management
courses.purpose: Choose training techniques from plant architecture and measured goals instead of technique names or yield promises.
courses.evidenceBoundary: Training changes geometry, tissue allocation, light interception and access; it does not create energy or guarantee yield.

units.title: Define the architecture goal
units.task: Write a measurable goal such as height control, branch spacing, support, access or light distribution before choosing a technique.
units.verify: The goal can be assessed after the intervention.

units.title: Map growth points
units.task: Record active tips, nodes, branch angles, plant height and stem condition before cutting or bending.
units.verify: The pre-intervention architecture is documented.

units.title: Wound and recovery monitoring
units.task: Track posture, new extension, wound condition and irrigation response after a tissue-removal event.
units.verify: Further stress is held until stated recovery criteria are met.

units.title: Canopy light distribution
units.task: Compare canopy geometry with PPFD or representative light observations before and after training.
units.verify: The result is evaluated by distribution, not only top count.

units.title: Airflow, support and access
units.task: Inspect interior humidity/air movement, branch support and service access after canopy fill changes.
units.verify: The canopy can still be scouted, serviced and supported safely.

exercises.title: Training decision worksheet
exercises.deliverable: Goal, plant condition, chosen technique, expected tradeoffs, measurements and recovery criteria.

exercises.title: Before/after canopy map
exercises.deliverable: A pair of architecture/light/access maps using the same measurement points.

courses.capstone: Evaluate one training intervention from stated objective through recovery and before/after canopy measurements.
completion: I define the objective before the technique.
I document pre-intervention architecture.
I use recovery criteria before stacking stress.
I evaluate light, airflow and access after training.

courses.title: Genetics & Breeding
courses.purpose: Document inheritance and selection while separating lineage claims, observed phenotype and measured genetic/chemical evidence.
courses.evidenceBoundary: A cultivar name or reported pedigree is not the same as verified genetic identity. Phenotype reflects genotype, development and environment; one plant does not define an entire population.

units.title: Identity and provenance
units.task: Build a line record with source, reported lineage, generation/clone status, acquisition date and uncertainty notes.
units.verify: Reported claims are labeled as reported rather than silently converted into verified facts.

units.title: Genotype, phenotype and environment
units.task: Choose three traits and list genetic, developmental and environmental contributors that could affect each.
units.verify: The worksheet does not treat phenotype as genotype alone.

units.title: Population and generation labels
units.task: Draw a simple F1, F2 and backcross pedigree and state what each label does and does not guarantee.
units.verify: Generation labels are not treated as proof of uniformity or quality.

units.title: Selection criteria
units.task: Define measurable selection traits, minimum observations and disqualifying conditions before evaluating plants.
units.verify: Selection rules are written before final choices.

units.title: Progeny and repeatability
units.task: Design a follow-up plan to test whether a selected trait repeats in relatives or progeny under documented conditions.
units.verify: The plan distinguishes an individual phenotype from inherited repeatability.

exercises.title: Pedigree and population sheet
exercises.deliverable: A traceable family diagram with parent IDs, generation labels, population counts and uncertainty notes.

exercises.title: Selection scorecard
exercises.deliverable: A predeclared multi-trait scorecard with measurements, notes and reasons for keep/remove decisions.

courses.capstone: Document one breeding or selection population with provenance, generation labels, phenotype records, selection criteria and a repeatability/progeny-test plan.
completion: I separate reported pedigree from verified identity.
I distinguish genotype and phenotype.
I use generation labels correctly.
I predeclare selection criteria and test repeatability.

courses.title: Harvest & Post-Harvest
courses.purpose: Assess maturity with multiple indicators and preserve quality through controlled handling, drying, equilibration and storage.
courses.evidenceBoundary: Maturation can be asynchronous and cultivar-specific. Stigma or trichome appearance alone should not be converted into a universal harvest percentage, effect prediction or fixed week.

units.title: Representative maturity sampling
units.task: Define where and how maturity observations are sampled across a plant or crop.
units.verify: The sample is not limited to one conveniently chosen flower site.

units.title: Multiple maturity indicators
units.task: Record trichome observations, stigma/flower development, plant/cultivar context and time trend separately.
units.verify: No single visual indicator is treated as universal proof.

units.title: Clean harvest handling
units.task: Map tool sanitation, lot identity, handling surfaces and hold/discard conditions.
units.verify: Harvested material remains traceable to plant/lot and handling event.

units.title: Drying as moisture transfer
units.task: Track temperature/RH and representative material observations through the drying period.
units.verify: The record uses time-series conditions rather than one room setpoint.

units.title: Storage and degradation
units.task: Identify light, heat, oxygen, moisture and handling exposures that could change stored quality.
units.verify: Storage choices are tied to controllable degradation risks.

exercises.title: Maturity observation sheet
exercises.deliverable: A repeated sampling sheet with site, date, magnification, observations and uncertainty.

exercises.title: Drying run log
exercises.deliverable: A time-series environmental/handling log with lot ID, observations and hold/release notes.

courses.capstone: Build a harvest-to-storage record for one lot that preserves maturity evidence, identity, drying conditions, handling and final storage decision.
completion: I sample maturity representatively.
I use multiple indicators.
I preserve lot identity and sanitation records.
I track drying/storage as controlled processes.

courses.title: Outdoor Cultivation
courses.purpose: Plan around the actual site, season, weather, water, biological pressure and pollen risk rather than copying an indoor schedule outdoors.
courses.evidenceBoundary: Outdoor timing and risk are location-, season-, genotype- and weather-dependent. There is no single universal month schedule or guaranteed zero-risk pollen isolation distance.

units.title: Site and sun characterization
units.task: Map direct sun, shade, access, drainage, wind exposure and nearby risk sources across the intended area.
units.verify: The plan uses observed site conditions instead of a generic sun-hours assumption.

units.title: Hardening and transplant
units.task: Create a staged exposure plan for moving protected plants into stronger sun, wind and temperature variation.
units.verify: Release depends on plant response rather than one fixed number of days.

units.title: Water and root-zone planning
units.task: Estimate irrigation access, delivery method, drainage and how soil/media moisture will be checked.
units.verify: The plan includes a repeatable observation or measurement method.

units.title: Weather, disease and support risk
units.task: Identify rain, humidity, wind and structural-load conditions that raise flowering or breakage risk.
units.verify: The plan includes monitoring and response triggers rather than weather folklore.

units.title: Pollen, pests and season records
units.task: Map nearby pollen sources where known, pest/wildlife pressure and key seasonal observations.
units.verify: Pollen risk is described probabilistically rather than as a guaranteed safe distance.

exercises.title: Outdoor site scorecard
exercises.deliverable: A site map/scorecard covering sun, water, drainage, wind, access, pests, pollen and disease-risk observations.

exercises.title: Season log template
exercises.deliverable: A weekly record for weather, plant stage, irrigation, pests/disease, support, flowering development and interventions.

courses.capstone: Create a location-specific outdoor crop plan that explains site choice, acclimation, irrigation, support, biological risk, pollen risk and the records used to adapt through the season.
completion: I characterize the actual site.
I harden plants gradually and observe response.
I plan water and support around local conditions.
I keep weather, pest and pollen risk contextual rather than universal.
